@ a call and a call under down 2 in one caller read their own times and do not mix: T * 100 + quot(T, 2)
@ the time under down 2 is quot(T, 2) at the even frames, held: 0 0 1 1 2 2 3 3
@ down 4 down 2 and down 2 down 4 are the quotient by 8, the two orders alike
@ down 4096: the shift is by 12 bits, the second tick is at the frame 4096
@ a part with no modifier under down 2 reads the time of its parent, which is quot(T, 2)
@ a chain inside a part under down 2 is down 2 down 2: quot(T, 4), the part running every second frame
@ a stage of sample / 2 of a part under down 2 reads the time of the part (§11.4: the same number in a slower stage)
@ a slow output that reads the time, under two parents with no modifier and under down 2, reads the time of the part
@ the replicas of a par~ under down 2 each read quot(T, 2), and the index is added
@ the arm of an if~ that is not chosen goes on counting under down 2, so it reads the time of the program when it is chosen again
@ the arms of a match~ have a time each under down 2, and both read quot(T, 2)
@ a reset makes the next frame the frame 0 for the part under the chain, in the middle of its tick too
@ the calls of process cut the frames anywhere, 0 frames too: the same time under down 2 and down 4 (§13.4)
@ an argument that reads the time is read in the caller: its time T, at the ticks of the part (T = 0, 4, 8)
@ a gathered argument is the caller's time of the 4 frames before the tick, and the head's own time is quot(T, 4)
@ a dealt output made from the time of the head is the frame number: the head at T = 4 c reads c and deals 4 c .. 4 c + 3
